user.title: Set up HA SOC
user.description: HA SOC centralizes user access, audit logging, dashboard permissions, device/integration vulnerability tracking, and a SOC-style risk dashboard. Only one instance is needed per Home Assistant install.

abort.single_instance_allowed: HA SOC is already configured. Only a single instance is supported.

init.title: HA SOC settings
init.description: Optionally push Home Assistant system detail (container CPU and memory, watchdog breaches, crash classifications, integration health, repairs, backup protection and Supervisor state) to Observe on an interval you choose. It is off by default and sends nothing until enabled. The ingest key is currently {key_state}; leave the key field blank to keep it. All other HA SOC settings live in the panel Settings tab, available to the account owner only. Submitting this dialog reloads HA SOC and re-registers the panel; reload the browser afterwards to load it.

data_description.observe_enabled: Off by default. Nothing leaves Home Assistant until this is on.
data_description.observe_url: The base address of your Observe server. https works for any address; plain http is accepted only for a private IP address or localhost.
data_description.observe_ingest_key: A host-bound ingest key that starts with wpi_. It is stored privately and never shown again.
data_description.observe_clear_key: Tick to delete the stored key. Leaving the key field blank keeps it.
data_description.observe_host_name: The host name the ingest key is bound to. Observe refuses data whose host name differs.
data_description.observe_interval_seconds: Seconds between pushes, from 30 to 3600. The default is 60.
data_description.observe_ca_pem: Optional. Paste the PEM certificate of the authority that signed your Observe server, or its own certificate when it is self-signed. When set, only that certificate is trusted for Observe. Leave blank to use the normal public authorities.
data_description.observe_cert_sha256: Optional alternative to the certificate above: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the one certificate your Observe server presents, as printed by openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256. Set only one of the two.

error.invalid_url: Enter a full http or https address without a user name, password, query or fragment.
error.insecure_url: Plain http is accepted only for a private IP address or localhost. Use https for any other address.
error.key_required_for_url_change: Enter the ingest key again to change the Observe URL. The stored key is never sent to a new address.
error.key_required_for_trust_change: Enter the ingest key again to set or change the trusted certificate or fingerprint. The stored key is never sent to a server you have just chosen to trust.
error.invalid_key: The ingest key must start with wpi_ and contain no spaces.
error.invalid_host_name: Enter the host name the ingest key is bound to, without spaces.
error.invalid_interval: The interval must be between 30 and 3600 seconds.
error.invalid_ca: Paste one or more certificates in PEM form, from BEGIN CERTIFICATE to END CERTIFICATE. A private key is refused.
error.invalid_fingerprint: Enter the SHA-256 fingerprint as 64 hexadecimal characters. Colons are allowed.
error.trust_conflict: Set either the certificate or the fingerprint, not both.
error.save_failed: The settings could not be written to disk, so nothing was changed. Check the free space and permissions of the Home Assistant storage folder and the log, then submit again.

abort.owner_required: Only the owner can change the Observe settings, because the access level is set to the owner only.
abort.not_loaded: HA SOC is not loaded, so its options cannot be changed. Reload the integration and try again.

admin_without_mfa.title: Admin account without multi-factor authentication
admin_without_mfa.description: The admin account "{user_name}" has no MFA module enrolled. An admin credential with no second factor is a full-takeover risk from a single leaked password. Enroll MFA for this user in Settings > People, or acknowledge this risk in the HA SOC Users view.

trusted_networks_permissive.title: Trusted Networks auth provider is permissively configured
trusted_networks_permissive.description: The trusted_networks auth provider is configured with a network range of {network}. This bypasses password authentication (and MFA, which trusted_networks never applies) for anyone on that range. Review the `trusted_networks` block in configuration.yaml.

http_insecure.title: Home Assistant is reachable without TLS
http_insecure.description: external_url is set to an http:// address, or use_ssl is disabled with no reverse proxy detected. Credentials and session tokens would transit in cleartext. See the HA SOC misconfiguration report for detail.

ip_ban_disabled.title: Automatic IP banning is disabled
ip_ban_disabled.description: `ip_ban_enabled` is false (or `login_attempts_threshold` is unset), so repeated failed logins never result in an automatic ban. Consider enabling ip_ban_enabled and setting a finite login_attempts_threshold in the http: section of configuration.yaml.

scanner_finding.title: Security scanner finding in {domain}
scanner_finding.description: HA SOC's integration scanner flagged {count} potential issue(s) in the "{domain}" integration's source. This is a heuristic finding — review it in the HA SOC Scanner view before taking any action against the integration or its author.

device_vulnerability.title: Possible known vulnerability on {device_name}
device_vulnerability.description: HA SOC matched "{device_name}" against {count} candidate CVE(s). This is a heuristic match — confirm or dismiss it in the HA SOC Vulnerabilities view.

misconfig_finding.title: {title}
misconfig_finding.description: {summary} Review this finding in the HA SOC misconfiguration report.

audit_chain_reset.title: The HA SOC audit chain was wiped or rolled back
audit_chain_reset.description: At startup, the on-disk audit chain head (sequence {disk_seq}) was behind the last flushed head recorded in HA SOC's store (sequence {store_seq}). The audit directory was deleted, replaced, or rolled back, and the records between those points are gone. HA SOC has continued the chain from the recorded head so the break itself is chained and auditable, but the missing history cannot be restored. Investigate what has filesystem access to .storage (SSH, Samba, or file-editor add-ons, or the host itself), then dismiss this issue.

stale_access_token.title: Long-lived access token unused for a long time
stale_access_token.description: The token "{token_name}" belonging to "{user_name}" hasn't been used since {last_used}. A long-lived access token never expires on its own — an old, forgotten one is standing attack surface if it ever leaked. Revoke it from the HA SOC Users & Access tab if it's no longer needed.

unclean_stop.title: Home Assistant restarted after an unclean stop
unclean_stop.description: The previous run ended without a clean-stop marker (classification: {classification}, gap {gap_seconds}s). HA SOC collected a forensics bundle at {bundle_path}. Top suspects: {top_suspects}. Review the bundle in the HA SOC Health view's Crash forensics card, then dismiss this issue.

tls_verification_disabled.title: Certificate checking is off for a device connection
tls_verification_disabled.description: HA SOC does not check the TLS certificate of: {connections}. Anyone who can intercept traffic between Home Assistant and that device can read the API key or password HA SOC sends and can answer with false data. Installs from before verification became the default keep their old setting so nothing stops working. If the device has a certificate your system trusts, turn on "Verify TLS certificate" for it in the HA SOC settings. If it uses a self-signed certificate, replace it with a trusted one where you can, or ignore this issue to accept the risk.

observe_key_rejected.title: Observe refused the ingest key
observe_key_rejected.description: Observe answered 401 or 403 to the HA SOC push, so the ingest key is wrong, was revoked, or is bound to a different host name than the one configured. Nothing is being delivered. Open the HA SOC options, enter a valid key and the host name it is bound to, and submit. The issue clears itself on the next accepted push.

observe_rejected.title: Observe keeps rejecting the HA SOC push
observe_rejected.description: Observe answered HTTP {status} to several HA SOC pushes in a row. This usually means the Observe URL points at the wrong place (404), the payload is refused (400, 415 or 422), or it is too large (413). The rejected payloads are dropped and sending slows down to at most one attempt every fifteen minutes. Check the Observe URL in the HA SOC options and the Observe server log. The issue clears itself on the next accepted push.

ingest_audit.name: Ingest external audit records
ingest_audit.description: Accept hash-chained audit records from a tool on this host after verifying the caller is the Supervisor and the per-source secret matches.

secret.name: Secret
secret.description: The source's pairing secret, pinned on its first accepted call.

records.name: Records
records.description: Up to 200 records in sequence order.

pair_terminal.name: Pair the Terminal app
pair_terminal.description: Called by the HA SOC Terminal app on start to hand HA SOC the credential its terminal server requires; accepted only from the Supervisor's context.

version.name: Version
version.description: The app's version, for the audit record.
